text: Unidentified flying objects took the upper Midwest by storm last night,
and this time the Twin Cities were not the exception.
Almost all Hennepin County and suburban police were looking through binocular eyes at the skies,
watched as many as three starlight objects, some flying in formation,
and traveling from the northwest to the northeast.
Now this is in the contrary direction to that of meteors.
The first sightings occurred about 12.23 this morning, the last about 3.30 this a.m.
The objects described as starlight pulsated in color from red to green.
Officer Bob Forrest of Shorewood told the Hennepin County Radio Dispatcher he had sighted a mysterious object,
and just minutes later, he said he was being chased down Highway 7 by a couple of stars.
His story was verified by other officers in the area.
The Air Force said their radar picked up no unidentified blimps.
However, they did have three B-52s on their scopes north of Crystal.
The sightings finally subsided about 3.30 this morning,
but during that period, during those three hours,
some witnesses said the objects would stop and then move off again at high speed.
The Minnetonka police said they saw a pair of UFOs near Lake Minnetonka.
However, it wasn't just officers in the Twin Cities area that saw the object.
West Dakota police officials reported seeing an unidentified flying object southwest of Mandan.
Both officers said the object was moving at a steady speed, but neither knew what it was.
Other UFO reports have come from Oklahoma, South Dakota, and Nebraska.
J.B. Eckert, KSDB News, in Minneapolis, St. Paul.
